prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: B002 was ranked first by all six of us, but unanimity is not itself the argument. The scientific case is a rare complete arc: proglucagon processing and the incretin effect, the truncated active GLP-1 peptide and its insulinotropic and satiety actions, receptor biology, and then drugs whose benefit has been confirmed in large independent outcome trials, including cardiovascular and renal signals. Originality is high, the mechanism is clear, and the interpretation is stable after two decades. A three-person physiology core of Holst, Drucker and Mojsov fits the cap and keeps the prize on the discovery rather than on one product line.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Credit for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is contested and I cannot resolve it from the record, and any trio excludes Knudsen, whose long-acting analogues are what patients actually receive, as well as pioneers outside the credited list such as Habener. A prize that honours the physiology but leaves out the drug design could be read as incomplete, and a prize that includes it displaces a basic-science laureate. If the committee cannot settle the Mojsov question, B002 becomes less clean than it looks from the opening tally.

responses.point: Sandberg proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen for B002, giving a basic-to-therapeutic arc, and leaves out Mojsov because her credit is contested.
responses.response: I understand the logic, since Knudsen's analogues made the clinical result possible. But I would keep the prize on the discovery of the physiology and the active peptide, and a contested credit is a reason to investigate it, not to drop her by default. Dropping Mojsov leaves the identification of the active GLP-1 form uncredited while rewarding its optimisation, and the Nobel tradition has more often honoured the discoverers than the industrial developers. I agree that Knudsen is the hardest omission and I would want the committee to say so explicitly in the record. If the Mojsov evidence turns out to be weak, Sandberg's configuration becomes my fallback.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks B001 second with Boyden, Nagel and Deisseroth, combining discovery of the channel with its demonstration in neurons, and notes that B051 (cGAS-STING) is a conceptually clean candidate that is perhaps somewhat early.
responses.response: I agree that optogenetics needs one discovery name and one neuronal-use name, but I disagree that Nagel is enough on the channel side. Hegemann's characterisation of channelrhodopsin-1 and -2 was decisive, and Bamberg's electrophysiology belongs in the discussion too. Choosing Boyden and Deisseroth together also splits credit within the neuronal-use group, and I do not see a principled basis for preferring them over each other except Deisseroth's broader programme. I also read B051 as promising but premature, because no approved drug has yet followed from the pathway.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius places B017 (TNF blockade) fourth, arguing that Feldmann and Maini form a clean pair with very mature clinical evidence, while flagging the missing Eshhar credit in B035.
responses.response: B017 is the cleanest two-person attribution on the list and the evidence is mature, so I take it seriously. My reservation is that the achievement is a drug class built on a known cytokine, and biosimilars and newer classes have blunted the sense of novelty, so I rank it below B001 and B035 on originality. I share her concern about the B035 gap: Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is not credited, and if the committee cannot fill that, B035 is weaker than its opening support suggests.

responses.point: Perlmann argues Knudsen's work is largely industrial and can be left out of a three-person B002 prize, and proposes Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel for B001.
responses.response: I agree on the core and on his B001 trio, which matches my own opening ranking. I would qualify the claim that Knudsen is merely industrial: translating a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly drug required real scientific invention, so excluding her is a defensible judgement, not an obvious one. We should not treat her omission as costless.

uncertainties: Whether the contested credit for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide supports naming Mojsov, and how Habener's role should be weighed.
Whether Knudsen should displace one physiology laureate on B002 under the three-person cap.
For B001, the fairest three-name split among Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenböck.
Whether B035 can be considered complete without credit for the original chimeric-receptor concept.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for the shortlisted candidates (B002, B001, B035, B046, B007, B016, B021, B051) from my profile. I co-authored the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and have co-authored works with Rickard Sandberg, but neither involves any shortlisted candidate or credited name.
